headline: Europe follows Asia lower as hot German producer prices add to rate fears

findings.headline: The overnight story held: European chip names take the hit, defensives hold up
findings.body: The Asian chip sell-off carried straight into Europe, with ASML, ASM International and Infineon among the heaviest fallers, while staples such as Nestlé, Unilever and BAT outperformed. Anthropic's record Nasdaq debut has not stopped the AI rout, and European shares are on course for their worst week since March. Leading and lagging is still split along AI exposure, not along regions.

sources.label: Investing.com: European shares near 1-month lows as Anthropic's debut fails to halt tech rout
Reuters via Investing.com: European shares on track for steepest weekly drop since March

findings.headline: German producer prices run hot, and UK shoppers stock up
findings.body: German producer prices rose 8.1% on the year in October against 7.2% expected, the biggest rise since February 2023, led by energy up 18.7%. That pipeline inflation makes a dovish ECB harder to argue for just as the Fed is seen hiking in December. UK retail volumes beat forecasts with a 0.7% monthly rise, but on households stocking up on long-life goods, which flatters the month rather than signalling stronger demand.

sources.label: ONS: retail sales, Great Britain, October 2026

findings.headline: Gold liquidation deepens as real rates climb
findings.body: Gold touched its lowest since early September 2025 this morning and is heading for its worst week in eight months, with silver falling harder. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson has backed further tightening, so a firm dollar and rising real yields are outweighing any safe-haven bid from the equity sell-off. Some of the selling also looks like investors raising cash against equity losses.

sources.label: CNBC: Gold heads for worst week in eight months on dollar strength
investingLive: Paulson says the Fed has more tightening to do

view: Our view: the overnight story held rather than flipped. With German pipeline inflation running hot and Fed officials backing more hikes, the rates side of this sell-off has firmer support than the AI-valuation side, so we expect long-duration growth stocks and gold to stay under pressure into the US open.
